summary.title: Algorithms (Jeff Erickson)
summary.one_liner: Free electronic edition of Jeff Erickson's algorithms textbook and related lecture notes, covering recursion, dynamic programming, graph algorithms, flows, NP-hardness, and randomized algorithms.
takeaways: The textbook is free to download in full, by chapter, or as a 472-page PDF (1st edition, June 2019) and is licensed CC BY 4.0.
Prerequisites are discrete math (especially induction) and basic data structures and algorithms (especially recursion); it does not teach basic data structures such as stacks, queues, or hash tables.
Chapters cover recursion, backtracking, dynamic programming, greedy algorithms, graph search, minimum spanning trees, shortest paths, flows and cuts, and NP-hardness.

Extra notes include advanced topics (FFT, linear programming, approximation algorithms), randomized and probabilistic topics (hashing, tail inequalities, streaming), and theory of computation (automata, Turing machines, undecidability).
Bug reports are submitted through a GitHub issue tracker; exercise solutions are not provided.
summary.summary: This page hosts a free electronic version of Jeff Erickson's self-published textbook Algorithms, plus lecture notes he wrote for University of Illinois courses CS 374 and CS 473. The page lists downloads for the full book, per-chapter PDFs, and a set of extended and "Director's Cut" topic notes, along with prerequisites and recommended background reading. It also explains licensing: the textbook is CC BY 4.0 and other notes are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, and bugs are reported via GitHub. The content is a table of contents and download index rather than teaching material itself.
